cards.explanation: The answer is fortieth. The writer says, "In the fortieth year, on the first day of the eleventh month, Moses proclaimed to the Israelites all that the LORD had commanded him concerning them." (Deuteronomy 1:3). Even the day is on the calendar, friends. Forty years, and somebody kept count.

The answer is explain, friends. In the land of Moab, "…Moses began to explain this law…" (Deuteronomy 1:5). He starts walking them through it, step by step, and I tell you, I have stood over a recipe card and explained it to a mixing bowl, so I respect the effort.

The answer is that the LORD said, "You have stayed at this mountain long enough." Moses recalls this word from Horeb (Deuteronomy 1:6). Next comes the word to resume their journey. I know that feeling, friends. Some of us need a voice at the door to tell us it's time to leave the junk drawer.

The answer is Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. The LORD swore He would give the land "…to your fathers Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and to their descendants after them." (Deuteronomy 1:8). This is a promise with a long history behind it. God says to enter and possess it, because He has placed it before them.

The answer is that the LORD made them as numerous as the stars. Moses says, "The LORD your God has multiplied you, so that today you are as numerous as the stars in the sky." (Deuteronomy 1:10). That's a whole lot of people for one man to look after, friends. It lines up with the promise made to Abraham, too (Genesis 15:5).

The answer is to choose wise men from each tribe. Moses says, "Choose for yourselves wise, understanding, and respected men from each of your tribes, and I will appoint them as your leaders." (Deuteronomy 1:13). The people pick, then Moses appoints. One man was carrying everything, and now the load gets shared.

The answer is True. Moses says, "Choose for yourselves wise, understanding, and respected men from each of your tribes, and I will appoint them as your leaders." (Deuteronomy 1:13). The tribes do the choosing, and Moses does the appointing. That's teamwork, friends.

The answer is in ranks from thousands down to tens. Moses appoints them "…as commanders of thousands, of hundreds, of fifties, and of tens, and as officers for your tribes." (Deuteronomy 1:15). Big groups, smaller groups, tiny groups, all the way down to tens. That's a lot of rungs on one ladder, friends.

The answer is False. Moses charges the judges, "Hear the disputes between your brothers, and judge fairly between a man and his brother or a foreign resident." (Deuteronomy 1:16). The foreign resident is named right there. Fair judging covers them too.

The answer is God, friends! Moses tells the judges, "Do not be intimidated by anyone, for judgment belongs to God." (Deuteronomy 1:17). Think about that. The big person in front of you is not the one holding the final say. That's why they can hear small and great alike without shaking in their sandals.

The answer is True. Moses says, "And bring to me any case too difficult for you, and I will hear it." (Deuteronomy 1:17). The judges don't have to guess on the tough ones. There's a place to take them, and that's a relief for anybody.
